stage_a.note: Both founders communicate pronounced and sustained positive engagement, smiling and energetic throughout.
They show very strong, sustained excitement about their product and business.
They are highly approachable, friendly, and positively oriented toward the investors.

venture.description: Silicone storage for markers, reusable straws, and bath scrubbers for kids.
venture.note: They are pitching Big Bee Little Bee, a brand with multiple silicone products for kids.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Introduces herself and her daughter, stating their ask and company name.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Says please alongside the company name.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains that making a mess is fun, but cleaning up is not.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Holds up a stop sign to emphasize the end of fun.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Describes the problem of lost marker caps and dried out markers.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Introduces the marker parker as the solution to the problem.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks how the marker parker works.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Explains that the marker parker grips the caps tight, allowing kids to remove and replace the drawing part easily.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Details the ergonomic shape and squishy texture that makes it easy to grip.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Reiterates that there are no more lost marker caps.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Shows how parents can easily wiggle out the caps to put new markers in, and asks who wants to help.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Mentions saving the planet from wasted markers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Concludes the pitch with the marker parker and their ask.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks Marlo if she made the drawings.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Confirms she made the drawings and that the words are quotes from the Sharks.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Compliments Marlo on doing a great job with the drawings.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Jokes about learning he is bald from her drawing.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Jokes about his drawing and asks Marlo how old she is.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: States her age.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Expresses amazement at her age.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Asks the panel if they want to try out the product.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Agrees to try the product.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Asks whether they are selling the holder or the whole set including markers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Prompts her daughter to answer the question.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Clarifies that they sell the base.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Confirms that it is a holder.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Agrees it is a holder.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks if the holder works for any type of markers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains that the current SKU fits broad tip markers, but they are modifying it to fit fine tip markers too.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Asks what prevents marker manufacturers from copying the idea themselves.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States they filed a provisional patent in November after her daughter thought of the idea.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Asks to confirm that Marlo thought of the idea.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Apologizes and confirms that her daughter invented it.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Expresses admiration for the invention.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Adds that she only helped her daughter take the idea to the finish line.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks for the retail price.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Prompts her daughter to state the price.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: States the price is fifteen dollars.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Repeats the price.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks what it costs to make the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gives the landed cost of the product.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Compliments the great profit margin.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks how they are selling and marketing the products currently.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains the history of the business starting six years ago with a towel instead of answering about marketing.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Prompts her daughter to share their other products.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Demonstrates the silicone scrubbie and explains its benefits for kids.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Praises the scrubbie idea.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks if she makes the straw product as well.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Describes the build-a-straw, explaining how it works and is easy to clean.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks what the hero product is and how much they are selling.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States the silicone scrubber is the hero product and gives last year's sales figure.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks if the sales figure was only for the scrubber.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Clarifies it was for the whole business, but the scrubber was 80%, despite losing inventory to supply chain issues.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks if they made a profit or lost money on last year's sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Provides the gross revenue and small net profit for last year.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks about the sales and profit for the current year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Gives the year-to-date sales figure and mentions lacking scrubbies in the first half.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Asks if she is making any money on this year's sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Admits she has lost a fortune and is down significantly this year.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks why she lost so much money.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains she invested a large sum of her own money to support her daughter's invention, despite having a fear of numbers.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Reacts with surprise to the amount invested.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Praises the young founder but criticizes the fear of numbers and the business problems, and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tells the investor he will want to take his exit back.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Agrees to see what she has to show next.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Shows a new food container product.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Explains that a whole apple can fit inside the container.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks if the product is individual silicone sandwich storage.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Begins to confirm but gets interrupted.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Criticizes the founder for inventing too many products instead of focusing on sales, and asks how many markers were sold.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: States they have sold over a thousand units.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Repeats the sales figure.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Repeats the figure in exasperation and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Accepts the exit.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks if she is running the business alone.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Says no and praises her daughter as her light.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Praises the mother-daughter dynamic but states the founder has overextended herself with too many products, and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Accepts the exit.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Admires what they have done but feels the approach is scatterbrained without a hero product, and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Thanks the investor for her time.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Advises the founder to act as a design studio and license products rather than building a business, and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Accepts the exit and thanks the investor.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Wishes them good luck.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Thanks the panel as they leave.

decisions.note: Fear of numbers is a bad story, wants a working business model to pour capital on, business has too many problems.
Founder has inventoritis, needs to focus on solving current problems rather than inventing new products.
Founder overextended herself, needs to perfect one product and make it a huge success before moving to the next.
Founder overextended, scattered approach with too many products, lacks a clear hero product.
Founder needs to be laser focused, strength is in design/inventing not building a business, should act as a design studio.

claim_conflicts.note: Founder claims $230k in sales last year, then says they grossed $97k last year.
